title: Store Rewards Sign up: Earn and Spend Coins
summary: Store rewards sign up in the Gerald app needs basic info. Earn coins from games, surveys, and tasks, then apply rewards to eligible purchases.
body_markdown:
Use this **How Gerald coins are earned** table to choose an activity you can finish today. Our[Play to Earn information](https://joingerald.com/play-to-earn) introduces that earning route, but the offer displayed in your app is what you should read before committing your time.


A game's required point might not be the moment you first open it. A survey requires reaching the final screen, an ad requires watching the full spot, and a task requires completing what its card lists. Don't substitute an action that looks similar for the stated requirement.


### Compare the posted amounts before starting


For a hypothetical after-work session, say you have **15 minutes** available. Open a survey offer and a game offer, then compare their posted coin amounts and completion requirements. Choose the higher amount only if you can reasonably finish its requirements in that break.


Before starting, use a short check:


- **Read the reward amount.** The amount you can earn for each task is shown in the app.
- **Identify the finish.** Find the required game milestone, final survey screen, complete ad, or task instruction.
- **Consider the effort.** Skip an offer if its requirements aren't worth your available time.
- **Keep a record.** Save the offer details so you can compare the promised amount with what posts.


A points system can be easier to understand when you separate earning from spending. BonusQR's explanation of[points-based rewards for coffee shops](https://bonusqr.com/loyalty-program/points-system) offers a useful comparison for that distinction, though its rules aren't Gerald's rules.


### Verify credit before doing more


Finish the selected activity, then refresh your coin balance before starting another. Keep the offer screen available, or retain a screenshot of its details, until you can verify the credit.


An unfinished survey or an ad closed before its ending can explain why a balance hasn't changed. Check completion before assuming the activity qualified, and don't treat the advertised amount as already earned.


A task card tells you what you could earn. The posted balance tells you what you actually have.


There isn't a universal coin rate you should use to predict every activity's return. Read each offer separately. Once coins post, choose deliberately between another worthwhile task and using the available rewards toward a needed purchase.


## Apply Rewards to Eligible Purchases


**Redemption is a checkout choice, not a cash-out.** The useful question is whether applying your available rewards makes a planned household order less expensive.


Suppose you need rice and dish soap before payday. Check whether suitable items are available in[Gerald's Cornerstore](https://joingerald.com/retail) , then compare the full order with your shopping budget. Rewards aren't a reason to add products you wouldn't otherwise buy.


### Review the basket before committing


1.


**Open Cornerstore and add an essential you already need.** Choose a suitable item rather than building a larger basket just to use rewards. Review the quantity and product details so you're buying what your household will use.


1.


**Apply available rewards at payment.** Use the amount the checkout makes available for that eligible order. Don't calculate spending power from an unfinished activity or assume a coin has a particular dollar conversion.


1.


**Read the reduced total.** Confirm what remains payable after the reward is applied. If the remaining amount doesn't fit your budget, reconsider the basket before making a redemption request.


1.


**Submit only when you're certain.** Rewards can be redeemed only by the account holder. Once you request redemption, **the request can't be cancelled or revoked** , so check the item, quantity, and remaining payment first.


### Recognize a successful redemption


A small posted balance can be useful now if it reduces a purchase you already intended to make. Leaving it unused doesn't help with today's essentials, but spending more than planned to consume it defeats the purpose.


**Checkout rule:** Judge the saving by the reduced amount you owe, not by how impressive the coin balance looks.


After applying rewards, check both sides of the transaction: **the order total should drop, and the reward balance should decrease by the amount applied** . Keep the order confirmation and review the balance if something doesn't match.


If we issue a Cornerstore refund, it may be given as store credit, except where applicable law limits that. Don't assume that returning an item will produce money in your bank account.


For a tight household budget, the final review matters as much as earning. An order is worthwhile when the essential fits your needs and the remaining payment is manageable, not merely because a rewards option appeared at checkout.


## Tips When Coins Are Slow to Matter


**81% of shoppers consider speed to rewards important, while 40% abandon programs when rewards take too long to earn** , according to findings reported by[Cornwall Live in its coverage of loyalty-card trends](https://www.cornwalllive.com/whats-on/shopping/loyalty-card-trends-2025-tendendo-9864588) . Waiting for a useful reward can make enrollment feel pointless, particularly when you need household basics now.


The answer isn't automatically to spend more time earning. Identify whether you're dealing with an incomplete activity, missing credit, an unclear rule, or a redemption restriction.


### Match the fix to the problem


-


**The task didn't credit.** Recheck its completion requirement and compare the expected in-app amount with your balance. Keep the offer details and contact support from the same account if the discrepancy remains unresolved. Opening another account won't clarify what happened to the original activity.


-


**The balance is too small to feel useful.** Consider applying available rewards to your next planned essentials order rather than stockpiling an abstract total. Don't add unnecessary items to make the reward feel larger.


-


**You can't establish a redemption rule.** Review the terms displayed in the app before doing more activities. Don't assume an expiration clock, minimum redemption amount, or ability to combine rewards that hasn't been stated.


-


**Redemption is suspended.** We may suspend your ability to redeem rewards during an account audit. We may also revoke some or all earned but unredeemed rewards if we determine that you violated the agreement. More earning won't necessarily resolve a restriction.


### Keep expectations proportionate


Your time belongs in the calculation. If you repeatedly abandon long tasks, choose an activity with requirements you can finish, or stop rather than continue chasing a balance that isn't helping your budget.


Keep records of participation and redemption when relevant to your circumstances. **You're responsible for any tax liability, including disclosure requirements, related to participation** in our rewards program.


A practical personal target is completing a task and applying a reward during your first week, rather than accumulating a large unused balance. That's a rule of thumb, not a promised earning timeline. It tests whether the program fits your actual shopping needs without turning rewards into another obligation.


## Choose the First Order Worth the Account


Choose a household item already on this week's list, such as dish soap, paper towels, or rice. Make that item your redemption target, not an excuse to browse for extras.


Open the app balance and work from **posted rewards** , not a task amount you haven't earned. At checkout, verify that applying the available reward reduces what you owe and that the balance reflects its use.


The finish line is an applied reward on a real essential, not a stockpile of coins.


If rewards cover only part of the item, a partial reduction can still help, provided the remaining cost fits your budget. Don't wait for a larger balance because a small saving seems less satisfying, and don't place an unaffordable order just to redeem.


Rewards don't need to be paid back because they aren't a loan. They also aren't withdrawable money, and you don't have to request a cash advance to complete this household-shopping routine.


Keep the account only if the effort produces value for purchases you would make anyway. Start with the essential you need most and the balance already available, then decide whether repeating the process is worth your time.


Gerald Technologies, Inc. offers an app where eligible users can earn coins through games and in-app activities, then redeem rewards toward Cornerstore household purchases. Visit[Gerald Technologies, Inc.](https://joingerald.com/) to explore the rewards process and choose a needed essential as your first redemption target.
